notes: Arrow cue rules (mw-e05.19). The bow twangs at the shooter as each arrow is loosed, louder the faster it leaves (a half draw is quieter than a full one). An arrow that lands on the world plays one impact-layer rule, the most specific that matches: its own arrow set for wood, stone and metal (a thunk into a post, a crack off a wall), a metal ricochet's ring, and otherwise the struck material's own impact set (sfx-impact-<class>), so no surface is silent; louder the more energy it carried, so a spent arrow dropping to the floor barely ticks. A creature hit is heard through its DamageApplied (the combat sheet's pierce-on-flesh matrix), so these impact rules skip creatures, except a glance: an arrow that fails to bite and ricochets off a creature plays the glance. An arrow with its own impact sound (a water splash, a noise rattle, a fire ignite) layers it on top in the payload layer. Not yet: the draw creak and the flyby past the listener (mw-e28.7), trail and impact VFX (mw-e29.11). Final assets arrive through the placeholder pack (e28.2) and the SFX asset groups (e38.28-31).
